question: Which part of the brain coordinates the sequence of a sneeze?
answer: The brainstem. A sneezing centre in the lateral medulla runs the sequence: a deep breath, a closed throat, then a blast through nose and mouth. A patient whose stroke damaged that area still felt the tickle in the nose but could no longer sneeze. The nose only raises the alarm.
move: Feeling an urge and carrying it out can live in different places.
trap: Assuming a blast this forceful needs the thinking brain in charge.
reference: Seijo-Martínez et al., Sneeze related area in the medulla: localisation of the human sneezing centre?, Journal of Neurology, Neurosurgery & Psychiatry, 2006
